channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Local de votação 2026: como consultar sua zona, seção e saber onde votar
item.description: Voters can check their polling place, including electoral zone and section, online or by phone for the 2026 elections. The first round takes place on the 4th, from 8am to 5pm, nationwide.

item.title: Como justificar o voto nas Eleições 2026? Veja prazo e passo a passo
item.description: Electors who cannot vote in the 2026 elections can justify their absence via e-Title, online, or in person. The procedure varies depending on whether the justification is made on election day or after the vote. The justification must be submitted within the deadlines set by the TSE.

item.title: Brasileiros votam em eleições acompanhadas de perto por Donald Trump
item.description: Brazilians vote between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, deciding if the country will follow Trump's conservative wave.

item.title: Flávio tem 50,2% e Lula, 47,4% em 2º turno em MG, diz AtlasIntel
item.description: An AtlasIntel/ Estadão poll in Minas Gerais shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading with 50.2% and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) at 47.4% in a hypothetical runoff, within the 2-point margin of error, indicating a statistical tie. The survey also reveals that 53% of Minas Gerais voters disapprove of Lula's administration.

item.title: Candidatos a deputado federal por São Paulo (SP): confira nome e números
item.description: The federal deputy election in São Paulo takes place on October 4, 2026, with 70 seats contested and over 34 million voters. Voters must enter the candidate's four-digit number and confirm, being able to check the photo, name, party, and status at the TSE.

item.title: Eleições 2026: votação é encerrada no Japão, onde filas foram registradas
item.description: Voting in the 2026 elections for Brazilians in Japan concluded with reported long lines and delays due to confusing instructions about required documents. Witnesses noted that volunteers struggled to guide voters, particularly the elderly, causing extended wait times. A total of 918,911 overseas voters are eligible, with 1,407 electronic voting machines across 134 countries.

item.title: Candidatos a deputado estadual pelo Rio de Janeiro (RJ): confira nome e números
item.description: The 2026 elections in Rio de Janeiro will feature 70 seats in the State Legislative Assembly (Alerj), with candidates identified by five-digit numbers. Voters must verify the photo, name, number, and party before confirming their vote and can check candidate lists and their status at the TSE. The Electoral Justice recommends writing down candidate numbers, as mobile phones are not allowed inside voting booths.

item.title: 80% das doações recebidas por presidenciáveis são repasses de PT e PL feitos para Lula e Flávio
item.description: Presidential candidates received R$ 164 million in donations, with 80% coming from direct transfers by the PT to Lula and the PL to Flávio Bolsonaro. Lula leads with R$ 77.3 million, while Flávio raised R$ 61.9 million. Flávio's campaign relies on 89% of its funding from the PL, and 97% of Lula's donations came from his party.

item.title: Eleições 2026 têm politização do STF, força do centrão, golpe baixo e feridas abertas; veja análises
item.description: The 2026 elections are marked by the strong presence of the STF and TSE, deepening polarization between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. Analyses highlight the Centrão's power in the Legislature and institutional tensions that may affect the election outcome.

item.title: Posso ir votar com camisa, bóton ou boné do meu candidato?
item.description: Voters are allowed to wear shirts, caps, or badges of their candidates on election day, as the TSE permits silent expression. However, any form of pressure, coercion, or active campaigning—such as distributing flyers, soliciting votes, or organizing group demonstrations—is prohibited near polling stations. Violations may result in heavy fines, criminal charges, and imprisonment of six months to one year.

item.title: Pesquisas de véspera reforçam aposta de Flávio Bolsonaro no voto útil
item.description: Pre-election polls show Flávio Bolsonaro statistically tied with Lula, reinforcing the strategy to mobilize right-wing and center-right voters for the first round. Flávio's campaign bets on support from voters of Ronaldo Caiado and Renan Santos, while Lula remains confident in advancing to the second round with a numerical lead.

item.title: Eleições 2026: transporte público será gratuito no DF neste domingo (4/10)
item.description: Public transportation in the Federal District will be free on Sunday (October 4th) for the first round of the 2026 General Elections, according to TSE Resolution No. 23,751/2026. The measure aims to ensure the free exercise of citizenship and also applies to a potential second round scheduled for October 25th.

item.title: Longas filas logo na abertura das urnas em Portugal
item.description: Thousands of Brazilians queued for hours at polling stations in Portugal for the 2026 vote, with slower lines in Lisbon and faster processing in Porto. The organization faced criticism over poor signage, but voting proceeded without major incidents.

item.title: Eleições 2026: entenda como funciona o voto de brasileiros no exterior
item.description: The 2026 elections abroad began before the first round in Brazil, with 918,876 Brazilians eligible to vote in 134 countries. Voting is organized by the Overseas Electoral Zone (ZZ) together with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and voters only choose the president and vice-president. The largest electorate is in the United States, followed by Portugal and Japan.

item.title: Da desconfiança à reta final: a caminhada de Flávio Bolsonaro no 1º turno
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) reaches the first round with 40% of voting intentions, behind Lula (45%), after overcoming internal crises, friendly fire, and doubts about campaign continuity. Initially marked by uncertainties and difficult alliances, his candidacy consolidated with Jair Bolsonaro's support and the PL as its base. The campaign was also impacted by fake news, investigations, and movements from allies like Tarcísio de Freitas.

item.title: Eleições sob chuva: confira a previsão do tempo no Brasil neste domingo
item.description: The first round of elections takes place under rain across much of Brazil, with storm risks in the South and heavy rains in the Southeast and Center-West, according to the National Institute of Meteorology.

item.title: Flávio se concentrou em Lula, STF e segurança pública na campanha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro focused his electoral campaign on criticizing Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and the Supreme Federal Court, emphasizing public security and corruption. Between August 16 and October 3, he posted 41 critical messages about Lula and 19 attacks on Supreme Court ministers, particularly Alexandre de Moraes and Flávio Dino. His strategy included controversial proposals, such as declaring criminal organizations as terrorist groups and chemical castration for rapists.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Brasileiros votam no EUA em meio à tensão com ICE
item.description: Over 265,000 Brazilian voters in the US face fear of voting in the 2026 elections due to intensified ICE operations. The Brazilian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Embassy are setting up 344 polling stations to reduce risks, but immigration enforcement concerns may lower turnout. Overseas voting is limited to president and vice-president.

item.title: Mais de 158 milhões de brasileiros vão às urnas para decidir futuro do país
item.description: Over 158.7 million Brazilians are eligible to vote in general elections that will decide the president, governors, senators, and legislators. Lula (PT) faces Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), while former president Jair Bolsonaro is ineligible and under house arrest after being convicted of attempted coup.

item.title: Eleições 2026: saiba onde votam os candidatos à Presidência
item.description: The first round of the 2026 presidential elections takes place this Sunday (October 4th), with 12 candidates voting across various locations in Brazil. Most candidates have their electoral residence in the Southeast region, including figures such as Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, and Romeu Zema. Voting times and addresses vary according to each candidate's home region.

item.title: Lula prioriza em campanha eventos de infraestrutura, saúde e educação
item.description: From August 16 to September 3, President Lula held 37 official events, focusing on infrastructure (6), health (5), and education (5). The campaign bypassed the electoral freeze by speaking at universities and construction sites, while issues like economy (4) and public security (1) align with voter concerns.

item.title: Eleições 2026: veja como acessar e-Título, horário e ordem da votação
item.description: The first-round elections in Brazil take place on October 4th, from 8am to 5pm. Over 158 million voters elect the president, governor, senator, and federal and state deputies. The e-Title app can be used as identification, but voters must check their photo in advance.

item.title: Campanha de Lula no 1º turno passou por crises e teve pacote de bondades
item.description: Lula's first-round campaign was marked by internal crises, investigations involving family and allies, and mutual attacks with Flávio Bolsonaro, who also faced controversies related to the STF and the Master Case. Despite the setbacks, Lula attempted to shift blame to his opponent, but dissatisfaction grew among allies toward the end of the race.

item.title: Sem utopias
item.description: The text criticizes the performance of the Supreme Federal Court in the 2026 elections, alleging that the STF shifted from defending democracy to supposedly favoring Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, interfering electorally against the current president.

item.title: Ensinar é o único ofício capaz de mudar o destino de alguém em uma só geração
item.description: The text criticizes the quality of Brazilian electoral campaigns, highlighting the superficial treatment of education and the prioritization of communication strategies over real proposals. It points out the lack of consistent investment in education by governments of all political stripes and emphasizes the importance of this sector for national development.

item.title: A jornada do voto e os riscos atuais
item.description: The text emphasizes the importance of voting in municipal and federal elections, warning about authoritarian risks and the fragility of the Supreme Federal Court. It reflects on Brazil's recent redemocratization and the role of institutions in protecting democracy.

item.title: Qual é o nosso sonho brasileiro para os próximos vinte anos? A flecha está na nossa mão
item.description: The text reflects on the Brazilian collective dream for the future, emphasizing the importance of public policies for access and inclusion such as the 'Lei do Boi' and Bolsa Família. It challenges myths about dependency and advocates for conscious voting as a tool for transformation. The author stresses the need to go beyond campaigns and demand post-election results, especially in education, income, and overcoming historical inequalities.

item.title: Quantos deputados são eleitos por estado? Entenda como é feito o cálculo
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies will have 513 lawmakers, with seats allocated per state based on the QPN and the Largest Remainder Method.

item.title: Autora de gol do São Paulo, Bia Menezes celebra título: ‘Torcida merece’
item.description: Bia Menezes, scorer of São Paulo's goal, celebrated the 2026 Feminine Brasileirão title, highlighting the team's journey and fan support. The final against Corinthians set a record attendance for women's club football in Brazil and South America.

item.title: Lula tem 46,7% e Flávio Bolsonaro, 43,8%, na véspera da eleição, aponta pesquisa AtlasIntel
item.description: Lula (PT) leads with 46.7% and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) holds 43.8% in the AtlasIntel poll of October 3rd, keeping a lead beyond the ±1pp margin. In a simulated second round, they are statistically tied at 47.6% to 47.4%. The race reveals a sharply polarized electorate split by region, education, and religion.

item.title: Flávio lidera disputa presidencial no ES, diz pesquisa
item.description: An AtlasIntel poll released on October 3, 2026 shows Flávio Bolsonaro leading voter intentions in Espírito Santo with 48.8%, against Lula's 34.4% in the first round. In a hypothetical second-round matchup, Bolsonaro leads with 51.7% versus Lula's 39.2%.

item.title: Os números da pesquisa AtlasIntel sobre a disputa entre Lula e Flávio na véspera da eleição
item.description: AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll shows Lula leading Flávio by 2.9 points ahead of the first round, with a simulated runoff indicating a technical tie between the two. Lula's government holds 46.8% approval among respondents.

item.title: Crise no STF, nó fiscal e Trump: profusão de desafios aguarda próximo governo
item.description: The next federal government will face a mix of historical and emerging challenges, including the STF crisis, the fiscal bottleneck, and international issues like Trump's influence. Experts emphasize the need to prioritize these topics on the national agenda to address structural problems affecting the Brazilian population for decades.

item.title: Lula tenta quarto mandato lutando contra desgaste de imagem após 44 anos em eleições
item.description: Lula, 80, is running for his seventh and likely final presidential election, facing image wear after 44 years of political highs and lows. His main challenge is overcoming voter fatigue and maintaining support in a polarized scenario.

item.title: Em estreia do Missão, Renan Santos fez campanha marcada por ataques e discurso radical
item.description: Renan Santos's campaign, representing the Missão party for president, was marked by direct attacks on Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, featuring an anti-system speech and radical positioning. The aggressive approach defines the candidate's debut in the 2026 presidential race.

item.title: Itamaraty corre perigo se Flávio Bolsonaro subir a rampa
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro proposed that his brother Eduardo become chancellor and promised 'a cleaning' in Brazilian diplomacy, a statement considered toxic. The suggestion drew criticism for threatening the independence of Itamaraty and Brazil's foreign policy.

item.title: Muralistas traduzem tensão eleitoral em retratos para a Folha do domingo de eleição
item.description: Muralists Paulo Ito and Carlos Eduardo Doy (Sosek) created portraits of President Lula (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) for Folha's Sunday edition released on the first round of the 2026 elections. The artworks reflect the electoral tension on the front pages and in the Politics section.

item.title: Lula tem 47,0% dos votos válidos ante 44,1% de Flávio, diz AtlasIntel
item.description: An AtlasIntel poll released on October 3, 2026, shows Lula with 47.0% of valid votes against Flávio Bolsonaro's 44.1% in the first round, with a one-point margin of error. In a potential runoff, the race is tied, with Lula leading by 0.2 percentage points. Government approval for Lula is negative, with 52.5% disapproving of the president's performance.

item.title: O pêndulo da Câmara: Centrão fica sem lado para tentar ampliar o poder
item.description: The Centrão struggles to unite in 2026, with divisions among parties supporting Tarcísio de Freitas and Flávio Bolsonaro. Scandals involving leaders like Ciro Nogueira and federal police investigations weaken alliances, while the Bolsonaro base remains fragmented ahead of the presidential election.

item.title: PT faz live de 8 horas e pede 1º turno para já encerrar a 6 X 1
item.description: The PT held an 8-hour live stream, dubbed 'Lulaço', to mobilize supporters and call for Lula's immediate reelection in the first round of the 2026 elections. The broadcast featured ministers, economists, and presenters, emphasizing the importance of advancing in Congress with the approval of proposals, particularly ending the 6 x 1 schedule. Despite the strong campaign, Lula did not participate in the live stream, while his opponent Flávio Bolsonaro has also used live streams as a mobilization strategy.

item.title: Datafolha: Lula aposta em mobilização na rua, e Flávio se mostra otimista na reta final
item.description: On the eve of the first-round vote, the campaigns of Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) seek a final boost for a potential runoff. Lula emphasizes street mobilization, while Flávio projects optimism about his electoral path.

item.title: Quem são todos os candidatos a deputado federal por Sergipe (SE) nas eleições 2026
item.description: Over 1.74 million eligible voters in Sergipe will choose among 141 candidates for federal deputy in the 2026 elections, with 20 deemed ineligible. The state will elect 8 representatives to the Chamber of Deputies in a single-round vote on October 4, using a proportional system.

item.title: Datafolha no DF: Flávio Bolsonaro tem 49% das intenções de voto e Lula 37%
item.description: The Datafolha poll released on October 3, 2026 shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading voter intentions in the Federal District with 49%, followed by Lula (PT) at 37%. In the second round, Flávio maintains the lead with 55% against Lula's 38%.

item.title: Flávio usa última live antes da votação para defender impeachment de ministros do STF e dar espaço a Douglas Ruas
item.description: In his final livestream before the first round, Flávio Bolsonaro urged voters to elect senators supporting Supreme Court minister impeachments and highlighted allied candidates, including Douglas Ruas, who criticized Eduardo Paes. He emphasized the need for an independent legislature to oversee the judiciary and pushed for split-ticket voting to shape the Senate.

item.title: AtlasIntel: Lula marca 50,1% contra 49,9% de Flávio Bolsonaro em 2º turno
item.description: AtlasIntel poll shows Lula at 50.1% vs. Flávio Bolsonaro at 49.9% in a hypothetical runoff, tied within the margin of error. Total votes include 5% blank, null, and undecided.

item.title: AtlasIntel: Lula tem 47% e Flávio, 44,1%, dos votos válidos em 1º turno
item.description: AtlasIntel poll released on October 3 shows Lula with 47% and Flávio Bolsonaro with 44.1% of valid votes in the first round. The survey, with a 1 percentage point margin of error, interviewed 4,945 voters between September 27 and October 2.

item.title: Capitalismo destruiu o jantar em família, diz Renan Santos
item.description: Renan Santos, presidential candidate from the Missão party, claimed in a podcast that capitalism weakens traditional habits like family dinners, linking it to industrialization and women's liberation. He used concepts from Deleuze, Guattari, and Mark Fisher to argue that the economic system reconfigures social meanings.

item.title: O que dizem as últimas pesquisas para presidente
item.description: The latest polling data for the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election shows a tightly contested race between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), with slight variations across different polling firms. The Quaest survey shows Lula at 46% and Bolsonaro at 45% of valid votes, while Datafolha reports Lula at 45% and Bolsonaro at 42%. According to the CNT/MDA poll, Lula leads outside the margin of error. The overall picture points to an open and unpredictable race, with minimal differentiation between the two main contenders.

item.title: Lula e Flávio chegam à eleição em campanha ofuscada por escândalos, crise no STF e até guerra santa
item.description: The 2026 election campaign is marked by corruption scandals and STF crisis, with Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro as the only viable candidates. Polls show a technical tie between the two, both facing high disapproval rates. The race is described as 'the rejeição dispute,' reflecting low voter enthusiasm.

item.title: Pesquisa Atlas: Lula tem 47% dos votos válidos contra 44,1% de Flávio Bolsonaro no 1º turno
item.description: The Atlas/Bloomberg poll released before the first round shows Lula leading with 47% of valid votes against Flávio Bolsonaro's 44.1%, a 2.9-point gap. In a simulated runoff, the two candidates are statistically tied.
